criteria.rationale: The claim that the first-open race may safely remain an inherited follow-up does not establish safe behavior for the newly introduced call. Linux regressions are verified; Windows test compilation was assessed statically because the filesystem blocked cross-compilation.
Reviewed common dispatch wiring and cleanup result propagation; no public API, event, file schema or MCP contract changes.
The helper is called from shared cleanup before the unchanged runtime inventory, covering all adapters.
Examined CLI/MCP integration and persisted cleanup reporting. Public formats and contracts remain unchanged; the separate Windows test-build regression is N3.

Mapped the selected design to R1-R3: a separate 200000-entry/8-GiB inventory addresses oversized Go leftovers without enlarging the ordinary runtime budget; Lstat and opened identity checks distinguish directory ownership; retaining the descriptor and checking unlink addresses the two prior removal races. The first-open defect remains separately reported as N4.

Examined the spec, requirement trace, review history, helper comments and matrix. They describe the selected budgets, unlink confirmation and platform fallback. The spec explicitly records the first-open limitation, which this review does not accept as a resolved risk.
The controlled implementation is a cleanup bugfix confined to the shared helper, unlink proof, regressions and validation checks; it preserves the ordinary inventory budget and public formats.

Compared the per-directory exception with increasing the global runtime limit or adding adapter-specific cleanup. Reusing the existing bounded remover in shared cleanup is proportionate; platform helpers isolate unlink-proof differences without speculative infrastructure. This choice requires a safe first open, whose current implementation is blocked by N4.

findings.action: The new FIFO regression calls syscall.Mkfifo from a test file compiled on Windows, where syscall.Mkfifo does not exist. The runtime.GOOS skip cannot prevent type checking. GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go list confirms this file is selected, and target-aware go doc syscall.Mkfifo reports no symbol. The sealed Windows check builds only cmd/pose and therefore misses this test-compilation regression. Move the FIFO-specific test into a platform-constrained file and add test-compilation coverage. The attempted Windows test cross-compilation was blocked by the read-only temporary directory, so this finding rests on source and symbol inspection.

A directory can be replaced with a FIFO after Lstat at line 622 and before OpenRoot at line 626. On the installed Go implementation, Root.OpenRoot opens the final component with O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC, without O_NONBLOCK or O_DIRECTORY (/usr/lib/go/src/os/root_unix.go:64-78), so cleanup blocks before reaching its identity check or returning an incomplete result. The new FIFO regression swaps only after contents removal and misses this first-open window. Although analogous existing calls share the problem and the spec records follow-up F1, this change introduces another reachable instance and does not satisfy R3 for that identity change. Use a nonblocking directory-only open that preserves confinement and add a synchronized regression before the first open.
